corrections.caveats: Enricher: harness defects in cbench.c (2006 SourceForge archive): the C-API scan row searches different strings on each side (strchr/strstr scan all of TESTSTRING1, which has no '.' and no "123", while bstrchr/binstr search "Dot. 123. Some more data." with hits at offsets 3 and 5), and the char* concat buffer is 15500 bytes but the test writes 15501, a one-byte overrun, so the baseline is undefined behaviour. cppbench.cpp uses the same inputs on both sides. Gotchas: bstraux bNetStr2Bstr reads past the buffer on a crafted length (unfixed upstream, fixed in the msteinert fork); open issues #27 (bsplitstr wrong on multi-character delimiters), #21 (CBString::format crash), #5 (int lengths), #11 (no move semantics); CBString's default constructor mallocs 8 bytes, with no small-string optimisation.

corrections.caveats: Enricher: the power-of-two capacity check is an assert, compiled out by Chapter_13's -DNDEBUG, so a non-power-of-two capacity silently mis-indexes. CPUs 2 and 12 are hard-coded and set_affinity exits on machines with 12 or fewer logical CPUs; 13x08 is Linux/glibc only (pthread_setaffinity_np). ops/sec counts items transferred; consumer() takes an int iteration count. In the optimised class capacity_ and the vector pointer share cache_tail_'s line and the buffer is not padded (rigtorp's SPSCQueue pads both). No tests for the queue.

Enricher: hash_benchmark divides the RDTSC total by loop_count*2 (200,000) but times 100,000 calls, so the printed cycles per operation are half the real figure (the ratio is unaffected). The timed calls are dominated by stringstream toString, ctime/sprintf timestamps and char-by-char Logger pushes; single run, array book always first. The MEOrderBook constructor leaves both std::array tables uninitialised (undefined behaviour; it works only on zeroed fresh pages). Open issue #9 (2026-07-04, no reply): price % 256 slots have no collision handling (SIGSEGV), and an order id >= 1048576 makes .at() throw inside noexcept (terminate), in both variants.
